description: Hand-derived islands (H1) cases, spec stretch S2. bars = [birth, death, peakCell, saddleCell, mergedInto] for death > birth, in reverse-sweep order. connectivity is the WATER connectivity; land uses the other. Heights row-major, row 0 north.

cases.name: cone with apex on the border: no island
cases.note: Apex (2,0) is a border cell, so the hill stays mainland until the apex floods.

cases.name: central cone: island once the whole border has flooded
cases.note: The highest border cell (14, h=1.5) is the last link to the mainland.

cases.name: ring ridge around a basin with a central peak
cases.note: Ridge (border, h=9) is mainland; basin floor h=1 except one gap cell 9 (h=2). The ring of water closes at 2.

cases.name: two hills joined by a saddle: cut off together, then split
cases.note: One island for t in [0,4) (peak 20), two for t in [4,7), one for [7,9).

cases.name: hill touching the border: not an island until cut off
cases.note: Border cell 10 (h=3) keeps the hill on the mainland for t < 3.

cases.name: strip: every cell is on the border
diagonal-only land contact, water 4 (land 8): one island
cases.note: Cells 6, 12, 18 touch only at corners; with 8-connected land they stay one island.

cases.name: diagonal-only land contact, water 8 (land 4): three islands
diagonal contact with the mainland, water 4 (land 8)
cases.note: Corner cell 0 touches the hill only diagonally, which keeps it mainland for t < 4.5.

cases.name: diagonal contact with the mainland, water 8 (land 4)
cases.note: With 4-connected land, cells 12 (h=5) and 18 (h=4) have no higher 4-neighbour, so they start components that die at once at cells 11 and 17: two zero-length bars, counted but not displayed.
